financing.summary: D.R. Horton funds itself with operating cash flow (US$3.5bn in FY2026), a US$3.3bn unsecured revolver agented by Mizuho, and investment-grade senior notes (A3 / BBB+ / A-); consolidated debt to capital was 20.8% at 9/30/2026 against a stated long-term target of about 20%, and it returned US$4.1bn to shareholders in the year. It controls 77% of its 570,600 homebuilding lots through land and lot purchase contracts (US$28.7bn remaining purchase price secured by US$2.6bn of deposits) and owns only about a 1.5-year supply. The controlled position is supplied by its 62%-owned lot developer Forestar (38,400 lots; 23% of FY2026 finished-lot purchases) and by a wide base of third-party lot developers that the company does not name; no institutional land banker is named in D.R. Horton's filings. The room for a land banker is mostly indirect: Horton has no set target for the controlled position, wants finished lots rather than self-development, and Forestar sells lots to unnamed lot bankers who expect to resell them to Horton (146 lots in FY2026, down from 927 in FY2025). With US$7.2bn of liquidity and an A-range balance sheet, Horton does not need land-bank capital for funding; the pitch has to be about returns, lot delivery and developer capacity.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light by purchase contract. Stated strategy: control a significant portion of the land and finished-lot position through purchase contracts and prioritise buying finished lots from Forestar and other land developers over self-development. Expects to own a one- to two-year supply of lots; no set target for the controlled lot position. 68% of FY2026 homes closed (70% in Q4) were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties, up from 65% in FY2025. FY2026 investment in lots, land and development was US$8.2bn; in Q4 it was US$2.0bn, of which US$1.4bn was finished lots, US$500m development and US$120m land (Q4 FY2026 call). Lot costs rose 6% in FY2026.

lots.note: Homebuilding segment only. total_controlled = owned + controlled through land and lot purchase contracts. 77,300 of the owned lots are finished. Controlled lots include 38,400 Forestar-owned lots (19,800 under contract, 18,600 under right of first offer). Remaining purchase price of controlled lots US$28.7bn, secured by US$2.6bn of earnest money (US$2.0bn / US$198.9m of that with Forestar). years_supply 6.8 = 570,600 lots / 84,202 homes closed in FY2026; the company presents 1.5 years owned and 5.2 years controlled (Q4 FY2026 investor presentation) and says it expects to own a one- to two-year supply. Prior year 9/30/2025: 591,900 total, 147,000 owned, 444,900 controlled (75%). By region at 9/30/2026 (owned / controlled): Northwest 10,500 / 16,900; Southwest 17,300 / 31,200; South Central 30,900 / 115,400; Southeast 27,600 / 103,300; East 28,600 / 104,600; North 15,600 / 68,700.

land_banking.description: Publicly traded lot developer, about 62% owned by D.R. Horton. Under the June 2017 Master Supply Agreement Horton's divisions buy finished lots from Forestar; at 9/30/2026 Horton had 19,800 Forestar lots under contract and a right of first offer on a further 18,600. Forestar sold 11,629 lots to Horton in FY2026 for US$1,291.5m (86% of its lots sold), about 23% of Horton's finished-lot purchases.
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m = remaining purchase price of Horton's lot contracts with Forestar (US$2.0bn, secured by US$198.9m of earnest money). Per Forestar's FY2026 10-K the supply agreement gives Horton a right of first offer on up to 100% of lots in Horton-sourced projects and up to 50% in Forestar-sourced projects, and runs until Horton owns under 15% of Forestar or June 29, 2037; Horton's consent is needed for Forestar debt that would take leverage above 40%. Forestar is separately capitalised (US$1.3bn liquidity, 6.7% net debt to capital) and its debt is not guaranteed by Horton. A Forestar stockholder derivative suit (Mississippi PERS v. D.R. Horton, Del. Ch., filed 2025-04-29) challenges lot-sale transactions between the two companies. Forestar's Executive Chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired 2026-10-31; CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman and CEO on 2026-11-01. Verification 2026-11-19: Forestar FY2026 10-K states revenues from lot sales to D.R. Horton of US$1,292.2m on 11,629 lots (vs US$1,291.5m in the description; the small gap was not resolved). Forestar Group Inc. is listed on the NYSE as FOR. Second source for the same relationship: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1406587/000162828026068139/a9302026exhibit991.htm, which is the source on the Forestar row in the land-finance scan.

land_banking.description: Forestar reports that its lot sales to customers other than D.R. Horton included 146 lots in fiscal 2026 and 927 lots in fiscal 2025 sold to lot bankers who expect to sell those lots to D.R. Horton at a future date. The lot bankers are not identified.

This is the only place in either company's filings where land-banker involvement in Horton's lot supply is stated; volume fell about 84% year on year.

land_banking.counterparty: Third-party land and lot developers (not individually disclosed)
land_banking.description: Horton controls about 401,700 lots outside Forestar through land and lot purchase contracts with land developers and land sellers, which it does not name. Contracts are generally non-recourse beyond the deposit, and most lots are expected to be purchased within three years. 68% of FY2026 homes closed were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties.
land_banking.note: Derived: 440,100 controlled lots less 38,400 Forestar lots; US$28.7bn total remaining purchase price less US$2.0bn with Forestar. Related deposits about US$2.4bn of the US$2.6bn total (cash US$2.4bn plus US$231.4m of promissory notes and surety bonds). Only US$78.5m of remaining purchase price carries specific-performance terms. FY2026 write-offs of earnest money and pre-acquisition costs on terminated homebuilding contracts were US$72.5m (US$114.3m in FY2025). The company says it has made significant progress expanding its land developer base and reducing self-development (Q4 FY2026 investor presentation). Counterparty names and any land-banker share of these contracts are not disclosed.

land_banking.description: Forestar sold 182 tract acres for US$8.2m in fiscal 2026 (42 acres for US$5.3m in fiscal 2025) to a third party that expects to sell finished lots to D.R. Horton at a later date.

competitor_links.relationship: Horton's in-house alternative to third-party land banking. Besides lot development, Forestar makes short-term 'lot banking' and 'land banking' investments in finished lots and undeveloped land that it sells mainly to D.R. Horton (lot banking projects: 116 lots / US$10.0m revenue in fiscal 2026, 348 lots / US$43.4m in fiscal 2025). Land held for future development is mostly under contract to Horton at carrying value plus 12% to 16% a year.
competitor_links.note: The 12% to 16% a year carry is the closest public price point for what Horton pays an affiliate to hold land; wording confirmed against the Forestar FY2026 10-K text. Forestar Group Inc. is about 62% owned by D.R. Horton.

competitor_links.relationship: Third-party lot bankers bought 146 Forestar lots in fiscal 2026 and 927 in fiscal 2025 with the expectation of reselling them to D.R. Horton. Forestar does not name them, so a link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon cannot be confirmed or ruled out from public filings.

ma.description: Acquired the homebuilding operations of SK Builders for about US$80m in cash: about 160 homes in inventory, 260 lots and a 110-home backlog, plus control of about 1,320 additional lots through land purchase contracts.
ma.map_impact: Adds scale in Greenville/Spartanburg within Horton's East region and about 1,580 owned and controlled lots. About 1,320 of those lots are controlled through land purchase contracts, so a third party (not named) holds them; the acquired local team is not named in the filing.
ma.note: Closed in fiscal Q1 2026 (October 2025), before the May 2026 ranking.

ma.description: Acquired the homebuilding operations of Clearview Homes for about US$40m in cash. Clearview operates in and around Detroit.
ma.map_impact: Takes Horton into Michigan: the state and a Detroit market appear in the FY2026 10-K (North region) but not in the 6/30/2026 10-Q, and Exhibit 21 lists 'DRH - Michigan CV, LLC'. A Detroit division leader and land contact should be added to the people map once named publicly. Homes, lots and backlog acquired are not disclosed.
ma.note: State count rose from 36 at 6/30/2026 to 38 at 9/30/2026 (Michigan and Idaho added); market count from 126 to 128.

gaps: Named land bankers or lot-option financiers used by D.R. Horton: not publicly disclosed. Filings refer only to 'land developers', 'third-party developers' and (in Forestar's reports) unnamed 'lot bankers'.

Public link to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none found in D.R. Horton or Forestar filings, releases or the Q4 FY2026 presentation. Trade press was not searched for these names (or for DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP, Brookfield, Värde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton), so this is a filings-only negative.
Split of the 401,700 non-Forestar controlled lots between finished-lot option contracts with developers, raw land contracts and land-banker structures: not publicly disclosed.
Homebuilding 'other notes' (US$249.2m): terms, maturities and security not disclosed.
Lender group beyond the administrative agents (Mizuho, JPMorgan, U.S. Bank) and revolver pricing margins: in the credit agreement exhibits, not reviewed in this run.
Counterparty of DHI Mortgage's US$500m uncommitted repurchase facility: not stated in the 10-K text (Royal Bank of Canada inferred from the exhibit list).
Clearview Homes acquisition: homes, lots and backlog acquired not disclosed; no press release found on the company site.
A business acquisition in the South Central region (US$53.1m paid, closed in the October to December 2024 quarter) is not named in the filings; it falls before the 2025 window.
Rating outlooks and dates of the last rating actions: not shown in company materials (ratings A3 / BBB+ / A- unchanged between the Q1 and Q4 FY2026 presentations).
Joint ventures: none disclosed at the homebuilding level.
